parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction that occurs when **A** is heated with $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: When aqueous $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is added to separate samples of **B** and **C**, effervescence is observed with **B** only.
parts.text: Complete the equation to describe the reaction between **B** and an excess of aqueous $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest why **C** does **not** react with aqueous $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ in a similar type of reaction to **B**.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
A student suggests a two-step synthesis to produce **B**, as shown in Fig. 5.2.
{{figure:figure_5_2.png}}
parts.text: Identify the reagents and conditions required in steps 1 and 2.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the type of reaction that $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ undergoes in step 2.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
**B** reacts with an excess of reducing agent **R** to produce **D**.
An excess of $\text{PCl}_5$ is added to **D**.
- A vigorous reaction occurs.
- Misty fumes are seen.
- Organic compound **E** is produced.
parts.text: Identify the formula of the reducing agent **R**.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Complete the equation to describe the reaction of **B** with an excess of **R**. Use $\text{[H]}$ to represent one atom of hydrogen from **R**.
